paper.title: Adaptive Pricing in Insurance: Generalized Linear Models and Gaussian Process Regression Approaches

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized Linear Pricing Model (insurance pricing with demand and log-claims GLMs)
unmapped: Dynamic pricing: action is a price p in interval [p_l, p_h]; reward is p*D(p) - C(p) (premium minus claims)
Learner observes demand and total claims separately at the chosen price
Demand mean h1(a0+a1 p) and log-claims mean h2(b0+b1 p) with known link and variance functions (canonical links in the analysis); the learner knows the link and variance functions
Noise: martingale-difference errors with bounded conditional variance and bounded gamma-th moment, gamma > 2 (Assumption A1)
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the insurance company knows the functional forms of the first two moments of demand and claims. ... E[D(p_t)]=h_1(a_0+a_1 p_t), Var(D(p_t))=\sigma_1^2 v_1(E[D(p_t)]) ... E[\log C(p_t)]=h_2(b_0+b_1 p_t) ... Regret(T) = E[\sum_{t=1}^T r(p^*)-r(p_t)]

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized Linear Pricing Model with delayed claims
unmapped: Dynamic insurance pricing with demand observed immediately and claims delayed by i.i.d. delays bounded by a maximum waiting time m
Demand and log-claims GLMs with known link and variance functions; the learner knows the link and variance functions
settings.definition_quote: We assume that demands are generated and observed immediately when a price is chosen, while claims might be delayed. ... We assume that (\tau_t)_{t\geq 1} is an i.i.d. sequence and is independent of prices and claims. ... Assume there is a maximum waiting time m

unmapped: Revenue r(p) = p f_d(p) - f_c(p) with expected demand f_d and claims f_c sampled independently from GPs with known means and kernels; additive kernel k_r = p^2 k_d + k_c
Price set is the interval [p_l, p_h]
settings.definition_quote: Functions f_d(\cdot), f_c(\cdot) are independently sampled from GPs with known means \mu_d, \mu_c and kernels k_d(p,p'), k_c(p,p'). ... The expected revenue function given a determined price p_t at time t is r(p_t) = p_t f_d(p_t) - f_c(p_t) + \varepsilon_t^r.

conditions: lambda_min(t) >= L_1(t) = c sqrt(t log t) a.s. for all t >= t_0
sum_{t<=T} ||p(t) - p(hat beta_t)||^2 <= K L_1(T) a.s. for all T >= t_0
unique optimal price with zero first derivative and negative second derivative of revenue near beta_0 (Proposition 4.1)

source.label: theorem_GLMBound
source.quote: Suppose there exists $t_{0} \in \N$, if MQLE $\widehat{{\bm{\beta}}}_{t}$ is strongly consistent and following conditions are satisfied: $\lambda_{\min}(t) \geq L_{1}(t) = c \sqrt{t \log(t)}$ a.s. ... $\sum_{t=1}^{T} \| \bm{p}(t) - \bm{p}(\widehat{{\bm{\beta}}}_{t}) \|^2 \leq K L_{1}(T)$ ... then the regret after $T$ time periods is $O(L_{1}(T)+ \sum_{t=1}^{T} \frac{\log(t)}{L_{1}(t)})$.

results.notes: The theorem states O(L1(T)+sum log t/L1(t)); with the fixed L1 = c sqrt(t log t) the paper states Regret(T)=O(sqrt(T log T)). The conditions are about the algorithm's behaviour and are assumed, not proved. The regret is defined through expected revenue, so it is recorded as pseudo-regret.

conditions: lambda_min(t) >= L_1(t) = c sqrt(t log t) a.s. for all t >= t_0
sum_{t<=T} ||p(t) - p(hat beta_t)||^2 <= (2 m_wait + K) L_1(T) a.s. for all T >= t_0
delays i.i.d., independent of prices and claims, bounded by m_wait

source.label: theorem_GLMDelayBound
source.quote: Suppose there exists $t_{0} \in \N$, if MQLE $\widehat{{\bm{\beta}}}_{t}$ is strongly consistent and following conditions are satisfied: ... $\sum_{t=1}^{T} \| \bm{p}(t) - \bm{p}(\widehat{{\bm{\beta}}}_{t}) \|^2 \leq (2m+K) L_{1}(T)$ a.s. ... The regret bound is $O(L_{1}(T)+ \sum_{t=1}^{T} \frac{\log(t)}{L_{1}(t)})$

results.notes: With L1 = c sqrt(t log t) this gives O(sqrt(T log T)). The dependence on m is hidden in the O.

conditions: Assumption 4.1: f_d, f_c are a.s. continuously differentiable with sub-Gaussian tails on the sup of their derivatives
tuning: varphi_t = 2 log(2 t^2 pi^2/(3 delta)) + 2 log(t^2)

source.label: theorem_GPBounds

results.notes: This adapts GP-UCB (Srinivas et al.) to the additive revenue kernel. Regret is defined in expectation but stated with probability 1-delta; the proof bounds the realised sum of r(p*)-r(p_t). The dependence on delta is hidden in the O.
